channel.title: The Income Tracker: new guides and updates
channel.description: New budgeting guides, bank CSV export walkthroughs, calculators, templates and product updates from The Income Tracker, the free UK income and expense tracker.

item.title: Update: Install it, and get a monthly nudge
item.description: The web app can now be installed to your phone or desktop and opens offline. A one-tap calendar reminder prompts you to import last month's statement, and the dashboard points you to your bank's export guide when a new month starts empty.

item.title: Update: Bigger help library, calculators, templates and comparisons
item.description: CSV export guides now cover 20 UK banks and card providers, plus a guide for PDF-only statements. New calculators for the 50/30/20 split, emergency funds, spend-per-day until payday, snowball versus avalanche and subscription costs. Free CSV budget templates that import in one step. Honest comparisons with Emma, Snoop, Moneyhub, YNAB, Plum and Monzo Trends. A site-wide menu, an RSS feed and a What's new page.

item.title: Free household bills tracker template
item.description: A free UK household bills tracker template: every direct debit, standing order and subscription with its billing day. Excel, Sheets, or import as recurring bills.

item.title: Free self-employed income and expense tracker template
item.description: A free UK self-employed income and expense tracker CSV. Categories match the Self Assessment self-employment pages, so year-end figures fall out of the sheet.

item.title: Free income and expenditure form template
item.description: A free UK income and expenditure form template in the layout lenders and debt advisers expect: income, fixed costs, living costs, debts. CSV for Excel or Sheets.

item.title: Free monthly budget planner template
item.description: A free UK monthly budget planner template as a plain CSV. Open it in Excel or Google Sheets, or import it into The Income Tracker for live totals. No sign-up.

item.title: Money Dashboard alternative: a free replacement
item.description: Money Dashboard shut down on 31 October 2023. The Income Tracker is a free alternative: the multi-account monthly view with no bank connection and data on your device.

item.title: Moneyhub alternative: what to use now the app has closed
item.description: Moneyhub's consumer app was sunsetted on 31 July 2026. The Income Tracker is a free Moneyhub alternative with no bank connection and data kept on your own device.

item.title: The Income Tracker vs Monzo Trends
item.description: Trends is free inside Monzo and adds one other bank free, more on paid plans. The Income Tracker is free, works with every UK bank via CSV and needs no Monzo account.

item.title: The Income Tracker vs Plum
item.description: Plum links your bank to save and invest automatically, with paid tiers from £3.99 a month and no manual mode. The Income Tracker is a free CSV budget with no bank link.

item.title: The Income Tracker vs YNAB
item.description: YNAB costs about £99 a year and teaches a rigorous zero-based method. The Income Tracker is free and simpler: a monthly ledger built from your bank CSV.

item.title: The Income Tracker vs Snoop
item.description: Snoop is free but does little until you connect a bank, and manual accounts need Snoop Plus at £5.99 a month. The Income Tracker is free, CSV-based and private.

item.title: The Income Tracker vs Emma
item.description: Emma's tiers cost £4.99 to £14.99 a month and lock CSV import behind Pro. The Income Tracker is free, needs no bank connection and keeps data in your browser.

item.title: The best free budgeting apps in the UK (2026)
item.description: Ten free budgeting apps for UK users compared on price, open banking, manual or CSV entry and who each suits. Prices checked September 2026. Our own weaknesses included.

item.title: Subscription cost calculator (yearly and five-year cost)
item.description: Free subscription cost calculator: enter your monthly subscriptions and see the yearly and five-year total, plus what cancelling a few is worth if you save it instead.

item.title: Debt snowball vs avalanche calculator (UK)
item.description: Free snowball vs avalanche calculator. Enter up to three debts with balance, APR and minimum payment, plus your extra payment, and compare the months and interest.

item.title: Spend per day until payday calculator
item.description: Enter what is left in your account, the days until payday and the bills still to come out, and see what you can spend per day and per week without going overdrawn.

item.title: Emergency fund calculator (UK)
item.description: Free UK emergency fund calculator. Enter your essential monthly outgoings and months of cover to see your target, the shortfall and the month you will reach it.

item.title: 50/30/20 budget calculator (UK)
item.description: Free UK 50/30/20 budget calculator. Enter your monthly take-home pay to see the needs, wants and savings targets, then compare them with what you actually spend.

item.title: How much should you save each month?
item.description: How much to save each month in the UK: the 20% guideline, why the first £1,000 matters most, the three-to-six-month emergency fund, and how to find your own number.

item.title: Track self-employed income and expenses for Self Assessment
item.description: For UK sole traders: what records to keep, the 2025/26 Self Assessment deadlines, the £1,000 trading allowance, and what Making Tax Digital means from April 2026.

item.title: How to budget on a variable income
item.description: A budgeting method for irregular income in the UK: find your baseline month, pay yourself a fixed amount, build a buffer, and keep a tax pot if self-employed.

item.title: Zero-based budgeting, the simple version
item.description: What zero-based budgeting is, a lighter UK version built around payday and monthly bills, how to set it up from last month's bank CSV, and where it goes wrong.

item.title: Budgeting as a couple with separate accounts
item.description: How UK couples with separate accounts budget together: the 50/50 split, the proportional split and yours-mine-ours, plus one ledger for both banks without shared logins.

item.title: How to find and cancel unused subscriptions
item.description: How to spot forgotten subscriptions in a UK bank statement and cancel each type properly: Direct Debits, standing orders, card continuous payments and app stores.

item.title: The 10-minute monthly money review
item.description: A ten-minute monthly money review: export last month's statement, import it, sort the strays, check recurring bills, compare with last month, move the surplus.

item.title: How to categorise bank transactions
item.description: How to categorise bank transactions for a budget: the ten categories that cover most UK households, rules that stop overthinking, and how to make sorting automatic.

item.title: How to read a bank statement CSV
item.description: What the columns in a UK bank CSV mean, what codes like DD, SO, FPI, BGC and DEB stand for, and why some banks split money in and money out into two columns.

item.title: How to import a PDF bank statement
item.description: Bank only gives you a PDF? You do not need a converter. Copy the transaction rows out of the PDF and paste them in. The app reads the dates, descriptions and amounts.
